newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: NAMIBIA SAYS TO LIFT FX CONTROLS THIS YEAR.
newsitem.headline: NAMIBIA SAYS TO LIFT FX CONTROLS THIS YEAR.

text.p: The Bank of Namibia is to lift most remaining foreign exchange controls on capital and current account transactions in 1997, it said in its 1996 annual report released on Wednesday.
"The remaining exchange controls, on both current and capital transactions, will be phased out gradually during the year", the bank said.

"While this could result in capital outflows that would put further pressure on foreign reserves and the balance of payments, virtually all remaining current account restrictions will be abolished," it added.

The balance of payments recorded a surplus of N$98 million, or 0,7 percent of GDP in 1996, similar to that in 1995, due to strong export earnings and an increase in transfers from the Southern African Customs Union (SACU).
It said, however, that SACU transfers were expected to decline in the near future due to trade liberalisation. "This underlines the importance of promoting an export-biased production."
The bank said its commitment to abolishing forex control restrictions was emphasised by its accession to Article V111 of the IMF.

The article precludes member countries from imposing restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions, or from engaging in discriminatory currency arrangements without IMF approval.

Namibia has already started divesting more authority to authorised dealers, has formulated policies to allow foreign controlled companies to borrow on the domestic market, and has approved direct investment by corporates in countries outside the Common Monetary Area.

Further requests by Namibian institutional investors to invest abroad are now sanctioned by the bank and it has introduced policies directed towards off-setting foreign liabilities against foreign accruals.
